messages.author: 0325eb8c004c41a5
messages.subject: Change of functionality in scale_x_log10() (version 0.9)
parts:
Dear All,

When I run the command:

qplot(carat, price, data=diamonds) + scale_x_log10()

The output is significantly different from version 0.8.9 and 0.9. In
version 0.8.9 the x axis has the scale changed to 10^{..}. However, in
version 0.9, the appearance of the plot is significantly different.

What's the best way of mimicking the scale change that version 0.8.9
gives?

Thanks

Colin

messages.subject: Re: Change of functionality in scale_x_log10() (version 0.9)
parts:
I think this is the same as the issue here:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/263

In the new version, the tick marks aren't shown as 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, etc, but instead as 1, 10, 100, etc.


Hadley, you said the solution was to use format=math_format(), but I'm not able to figure out how to make it work. For example, I think you'd want something like this:

qplot(carat, price, data=diamonds) +
    scale_x_continuous(trans = "log10", labels = math_format(expr=10^log10(.x)))

... except that you would want the log10() part of the expression to be evaluated, not printed. Is there a way to do that?

-Winston

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Change of functionality in scale_x_log10() (version 0.9)
parts:
If you want the old labeling, a 'simple' way to do it in 0.9.0 is to
transform carat and then use math_format() to get the labeling to look
like 0.8.9:

library('ggplot2') # 0.9.0 development version
library('scales')

qplot(log10(carat), price, data = diamonds) +
scale_x_continuous(name = 'carat', labels = math_format(10^.x))

The advantage of using log10(carat) in the qplot call is that the
default breaks from qplot() are the exponents you want to pass to
math_format().

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Change of functionality in scale_x_log10() (version 0.9)
parts:
I tried all sorts of stuff when plotting carat vs. price:
trans_breaks(), coordinate transformation followed by
scale_x_continuous(), a half dozen others. The closest I got was this:

> trans_breaks('log10', function(x) 10^x)(diamonds$carat)
[1] 0.1584893 0.2511886 0.3981072 0.6309573 1.0000000 1.5848932 2.5118864
[8] 3.9810717 6.3095734
log10(trans_breaks('log10', function(x) 10^x)(diamonds$carat))
[1] -0.8 -0.6 -0.4 -0.2 0.0 0.2 0.4 0.6 0.8

This gives the right values for the exponents, but it's a pretty
convoluted way of getting them. The problem is that if you use this in
conjunction with scale_x_continuous's labels = argument using
math_format(), the position of the tick marks is all wrong. Try this:

lb <- log10(trans_breaks('log10', function(x) 10^x)(diamonds$carat))
qplot(carat, price, data = diamonds) +
scale_x_continuous(breaks = 10^lb, labels = math_format(10^.x)(lb))

This is basically a reflection of your tick mark positions around 1.
If there's a way to get a linear scale with math_format() using
scale_x_continuous() and its breaks = and values = arguments, I
haven't found it yet.

I *think* the problem is that qplot() is plotting in the original
metric for carat, so there's no way it can render a linear scale in
the exponents. Here's one example I tried with coord_trans():

qplot(carat, price, data = diamonds) + coord_trans(xtrans = 'log10')
last_plot() + scale_x_continuous(breaks = lb, labels = math_format(10^.x)(lb))

But after a little thought just now, this got me closer:

last_plot() + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 10^lb, labels =
math_format(10^.x)(lb))

It looks as though a little massaging of the exponents-as-breaks
vector should do it, but I think that trans_breaks() is supposed to do
the work. I need to play with that some more until I get it right.

Dennis
